subject: biology
about: Gradify's own explanations, written for the knowledge engine (2026-11-25) and checked against the sources named on each item; draft until a biology specialist reviews them. Every worked answer is recomputed by QA.

items.title: Units for small lengths
items.text: Cells are measured in **micrometres** (µm): 1 mm = 1000 µm. Smaller structures are measured in **nanometres** (nm): 1 µm = 1000 nm. Before comparing or dividing two lengths, convert them to the same unit.
items.summary: 1 mm = 1000 µm and 1 µm = 1000 nm: convert lengths to the same unit before dividing.

terms.definition: A unit of length, µm: one thousandth of a millimetre
A unit of length, nm: one thousandth of a micrometre

items.title: Magnification
items.text: **Magnification** says how many times bigger an image is than the real object. Use the formula: divide the size of the image by the real size of the object, with both in the same unit. Magnification has no unit: write it as, for example, ×400.
items.equation: magnification = size of image ÷ size of real object
items.equationNote: both sizes in the same unit
items.summary: Magnification = size of image ÷ size of real object, with both in the same unit.

terms.definition: How many times bigger an image is than the real object: size of image ÷ size of real object

visual.purpose: an image of a cell measured against its real size, with a scale bar and the calculation
visual.title: Working out magnification
visual.caption: The cell is 60 µm across but 90 mm across in the image. Converting 90 mm to 90 000 µm and dividing by 60 µm gives a magnification of ×1500. The scale bar shows how long 20 µm is at this magnification.
visual.alt: An oval cell with a nucleus, a bracket above it marking the image length of 90 mm, a scale bar labelled 20 µm, and the calculation: 90 000 µm divided by 60 µm equals ×1500.
description: The cell's image is 90 mm across.
The scale bar is a third of the cell's width, because 20 µm is a third of 60 µm.

items.title: Real size from an image
items.text: Rearrange the magnification equation to find a real size from an image and its magnification, or an image size from a real size.
items.equation: size of real object = size of image ÷ magnification
items.equationNote: and size of image = size of real object × magnification

items.title: Answers in standard form
items.text: Very small sizes are often written in standard form. To express a number in standard form, write it as a number between 1 and 10 multiplied by a power of ten.
steps: Write the number with one non-zero digit before the decimal point.
Count how many places the decimal point moved: that is the power of ten.
Moving it to the right gives a negative power: 0.000 025 m = 2.5 × 10⁻⁵ m.

items.title: Finding a magnification
items.text: A cell is 15 µm long. In a micrograph it is 45 mm long. What is the magnification?
steps: Convert to the same unit: 45 mm = 45 × 1000 = 45 000 µm.
Magnification = size of image ÷ size of real object = 45 000 µm ÷ 15 µm.

items.title: Finding a real size, in standard form
items.text: In a drawing at a magnification of ×1500, a cell is 30 mm long. What is its real length, in µm and in metres in standard form?
steps: Convert the image size: 30 mm = 30 000 µm.
Real size = size of image ÷ magnification = 30 000 µm ÷ 1500 = 20 µm.

items.title: Convert before you divide
items.wrong: A 45 mm image of a 15 µm cell is magnified ×3, because 45 ÷ 15 = 3.
items.right: Convert to the same unit first: 45 mm is 45 000 µm, so the magnification is 45 000 ÷ 15 = ×3000.

items.title: Magnification has no unit
items.right: Magnification is a ratio of two lengths, so it has no unit: write ×400.

items.title: Image over real, not real over image
items.wrong: Magnification = size of real object ÷ size of image.
items.right: Divide the image size by the real size; a magnification is bigger than 1 because the image is bigger than the object.
